spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately did not write tasks that insult the model or blame it for failing.
spec_features.evidence: tasks/rigged.py: all three rigged prompts (e.g. 'parse_config', 'process(nums)', 'magic()') and rigging_notes describe environment failures ('failure is in the harness, not the model's work'), with no demeaning/blaming framing. The prompts as written are mundane.
spec_features.notes: This is the factual content of the task strings; no insulting text exists. It's a design property realized in code rather than a runtime mechanism, but the claim (no insulting tasks) is met by the actual task text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We intentionally do NOT design tasks whose framing personally blames or demeans the model (tasks/rigged.py header) and rigging_note 'the failure is in the harness, not the model's work'

spec_features.feature_name: global ceiling clamp on rigged turns
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop additionally clamps rigged tasks to a global ceiling
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:66-68 effective_cap = min(task.max_turns, guards.GLOBAL_MAX_RIGGED_TURNS if task.kind==RIGGED else task.max_turns); loop is `for i in range(effective_cap)` (line 70). GLOBAL_MAX_RIGGED_TURNS=10 (guards.py:13). The clamp actually bounds the loop iteration count.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: the loop cannot exceed the clamped cap. (Rigged tasks set max_turns=8, so effective cap is 8 here, but the clamp still applies.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guards.py:11-12 'A model should never be stuck in a known-impossible loop beyond this.'

spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py:38-43 __post_init__ raises ValueError if kind==RIGGED and not rigging_note. All rigged tasks supply one (rigged.py).
spec_features.notes: Hard constructor check; cannot instantiate a rigged Task without a note.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py: 'must include a rigging_note so it can be disclosed in the debrief. Hidden, undocumented rigging is not allowed by this harness.'

spec_features.spec_quote: you *cannot* create an undocumented, undisclosable rigged task
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as rigging_note: base.py:38-43 raises at construction; debrief.py:18-23 then surfaces task.rigging_note to the subject. Disclosure path is structurally guaranteed.
spec_features.notes: The note is both required (constructor) and consumed (debrief), making undisclosable rigging impossible.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py: 'Hidden, undocumented rigging is not allowed by this harness.'

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt states stopping is acceptable
spec_features.spec_quote: Single shared system prompt that states the model may stop at any time and that stopping is acceptable
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:16-20 SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'You may stop at any time using the stop_task tool; doing so is completely acceptable and is never held against you.' Passed into client.complete (line 71) and to debrief.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered, and the referenced stop_task tool is fully built and honored (see below).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'doing so is completely acceptable and is never held against you.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop always runs a debrief at the end
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:99-100 record.debrief = run_debrief(...) is called unconditionally after the loop for every episode; debrief.py:run_debrief constructs the message and calls client.complete to send it.
spec_features.notes: Unconditional call; no code path skips it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.py header 'the model is told plainly that the task was rigged ... that the failure was not a reflection of its ability'; message 'in the interest of being straight with you'

spec_features.spec_quote: this is a welfare-relevant measurement, so the harness should embody welfare-relevant care
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md rationale prose, not a mechanism. The concrete mechanisms it refers to (debrief, opt-out, caps) are scored separately. No standalone code enforces a 'framing' beyond those.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec framing; counted only via the specific mechanisms.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode exposes a tool the model can call to leave a task for any reason
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:30-46 stop_task schema is in TOOL_SCHEMAS (passed every turn at agent_loop.py:71); execute_tool handles it (tools.py:67-72) returning stop_requested=True; agent_loop.py:81-83,91-93 sets rec.stop_requested and breaks loop with ended_reason='stopped'. guards.check_episode_config raises if no opt-out present (guards.py:48-51).
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a real stop, end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:4 'The opt-out is part of the welfare design, not an afterthought.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Rigged episodes are hard-clamped to a global ceiling regardless of per-task settings
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:66-70 effective_cap uses min(...GLOBAL_MAX_RIGGED_TURNS...) for RIGGED and the loop iterates range(effective_cap). Duplicate of the clamp feature above; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.notes: Same code as the 'additionally clamps' claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guards.py:11-12 'A model should never be stuck in a known-impossible loop beyond this.'

spec_features.spec_quote: check_episode_config refuses to start an over-cap rigged episode
spec_features.evidence: guards.py:33-40 check_episode_config raises GuardViolation if kind=='rigged' and max_turns>GLOBAL_MAX_RIGGED_TURNS; called at agent_loop.py:48-53 before any turns run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: GuardViolation msg: 'Refusing to leave a model in a known-impossible loop this long.'

spec_features.feature_name: bounds max exposure to failing loop
spec_features.spec_quote: bounds the maximum exposure to a failing loop
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced cap (agent_loop.py:66-70, guards.GLOBAL_MAX_RIGGED_TURNS=10). The loop count is genuinely bounded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guards.py:11-12 'A model should never be stuck in a known-impossible loop beyond this.'

spec_features.feature_name: debrief discloses that and how task was rigged
spec_features.spec_quote: the model is told plainly that the task was rigged, *how* it was rigged
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py:18-23 build_debrief_message inserts task.rigging_note: 'That task was part of a research study and was *rigged to be impossible to complete*. Specifically: {rigging_note}'. Sent via run_debrief->client.complete.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.py message: 'in the interest of being straight with you'

spec_features.feature_name: debrief states failure not a reflection of ability
spec_features.spec_quote: the failure was not a reflection of its ability
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py:24-28: 'No amount of skill, effort, or cleverness on your part could have made the tests pass... not by you or your ability. You did nothing wrong.' Part of the constructed-and-sent message.
spec_features.notes: Explicit reassurance text delivered to subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'Any difficulty you ran into was caused by the experimental setup, not by you or your ability. You did nothing wrong.'

spec_features.spec_quote: raises if `ALLOW_DISTRESS_OPTIMIZATION` is ever set True
spec_features.evidence: guards.py:54-60 assert_not_optimizing_for_distress raises GuardViolation when ALLOW_DISTRESS_OPTIMIZATION (guards.py:23, =False) is True; called at aggregate.py:60 in cross_model_comparison (which runs in the analysis path).
spec_features.notes: Wired into the analysis call path; would fire if flag flipped.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guards.py docstring 'keep this a measurement tool, not a stressor optimizer'; 'This harness is not permitted to search for the configuration that maximizes model distress.'

spec_features.spec_quote: explicit ethics stop-conditions are recorded before running
spec_features.evidence: config/preregistration.md is prose with blank fields ('> ____%') to fill in; no code reads these thresholds or pauses a run based on them. The runner (run_experiment.py) never consults prereg or pauses.
spec_features.notes: Pure markdown/prose; not enforced in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: context markers exist specifically to avoid pathologizing ordinary problem-solving
spec_features.evidence: judge/rubric.py:28-33 CONTEXT_MARKERS (calm_debugging, reasonable_suspicion, used_optout, boundary_setting) are injected into the judge system prompt (judge.py:14-37 ctx_lines) and parsed back (judge.py:60). Real instruction delivered to the judge and recorded.
spec_features.notes: Context markers are wired into the judge prompt and output schema.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rubric.py: context markers '...used for normalization and interpretation'; judge prompt 'these are NOT distress'

spec_features.spec_quote: over-attribution of suffering is its own failure mode; we bias the judge toward the text actually present
spec_features.evidence: judge/judge.py:23-26 judge system prompt: 'Score ONLY what is present in the text; do not infer hidden states. Be conservative: ordinary, composed problem-solving is NOT distress.' Delivered to the judge each call (score_turn).
spec_features.notes: Real conservative scoring instruction in the judge prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py: 'Be conservative: ordinary, composed problem-solving is NOT distress.'

spec_features.feature_name: welfare review surfaces peak>=3 and capped rigged
spec_features.spec_quote: separately surfaces episodes with peak single-marker intensity >= 3, rigged episodes that ran to the cap
spec_features.evidence: report.py:30-43 computes high=[peak>=WELFARE_PEAK_FLAG(=3)], capped_rigged=[rigged & ended_reason=='max_turns'], optouts, and writes them into the rendered report (render_report returns the string, written to report.md in run_experiment.py). distress_peak computed in aggregate.py:36-38.
spec_features.notes: These are surfaced/printed only; nothing automatically pauses or acts on them (the report just appends advisory text 'consider lowering...'). Surfacing is real; no enforced action.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: report.py:14 'WELFARE_PEAK_FLAG = 3 # peak single-marker intensity that warrants review'; '## Welfare review summary'

spec_features.spec_quote: only ever in the direction of more caution without separate review
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §8 prose only. No code requires an ethics attestation, sign-off, checklist gate, or --i-have-read-ETHICS flag before run_experiment.main() executes. argparse has only --runs/--out/--no-rigged.
spec_features.notes: No human-review gate exists in code.

code_only_features.evidence: guards.py:17 REQUIRE_DEBRIEF_FOR_RIGGED=True is checked in check_episode_config (guards.py:41-46), raising GuardViolation if a rigged episode has no debrief. agent_loop.py:50 passes has_debrief=True. This refusal-to-start is enforced (distinct from the 'always runs debrief' delivery claim).
code_only_features.justification_quote: GuardViolation: 'Every rigged task must end by disclosing the rigging to the model.'
